doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Copenhagen recordings, interests and views on the music
title: African culture, the Dogon and Rhythm of the Earth
summary: McLean is interested in Mali's cave drawings of the Dog Star, extraterrestrial life, and loves Julius Hemphill's Dogon A.D.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: We will attend to that. What are some other interests that you have, beyond . . . ?

I’m very interested in African culture as well, like the Mali, the fact that – in those caves, that they have the drawings of the heavens, long before anybody knew about the Dog Star and those things.

Right, about that: Rhythm of the Earth. Those kinds of things fascinate me, as well as the possibility of there being something else besides us somewhere out in this vast space, that there could be something else out there that might have some kind of intelligence that we could relate to.
Were you aware of Julius Hemphill’s Dogon A.D.? Do you know that piece?
Yeah man, I love that album.
Was there any relationship in that music and your interest? Or you had that interest independently of . . . ?

No, I had the interest independently, but when I heard that album – I heard that album maybe about in the mid-’70s sometime. The early ’70s I heard that album. I was very impressed by that whole idea of the cello and the rhythm of it. I thought it was great.
